headers.//: frame-ancestors replaces X-Frame-Options; script-src allows inline because the theme script must run before first paint to prevent a white flash, and the JSON-LD block is inline by definition. THE GOOGLE HOSTS ARE NOT OPTIONAL: this policy was 'self' everywhere and it silently broke the whole dashboard — connect-src governs the identitytoolkit/securetoken/firestore endpoints, frame-src governs the __/auth/handler iframe signInWithPopup opens, and script-src governs apis.google.com. Sign-in failed with a generic 'try again' and no clue, because a CSP block surfaces as an opaque auth error. Each allowance is pinned to an exact Google host rather than widened to https:. If sign-in or data loading ever breaks again, read the browser console for a CSP violation first.
headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://apis.google.com https://www.gstatic.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://identitytoolkit.googleapis.com https://securetoken.googleapis.com https://firestore.googleapis.com; frame-src https://*.firebaseapp.com https://accounts.google.com; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; upgrade-insecure-requests

headers.//: Next emits the share card as an extensionless file named `opengraph-image`. Static hosting types files by extension, so without this it goes out as application/octet-stream and social scrapers drop the card — og:image:type in the HTML does not override the real header.
Content-hashed filenames — safe to cache forever. Fonts are hashed by next/font, so they fall under this too.
